candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — invasive-device infection prevention and safe equipment/device management
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — central-line necessity review
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize prompt removal of a no-longer-needed central venous catheter as a key CLABSI-prevention strategy distinct from insertion-bundle elements.

options.A: Promptly communicate that the catheter is no longer necessary and facilitate removal according to the care plan and facility process
options.B: Leave the catheter in place indefinitely because infection risk does not increase with unnecessary catheter days
options.C: Replace the catheter routinely with a new central line solely to prevent infection, even though central access is no longer needed
options.D: Keep the catheter until discharge because insertion-site care eliminates the infection risk of an unnecessary line

candidate.rationale: Central-line infection prevention includes both safe insertion and limiting unnecessary catheter exposure. CDC guidance emphasizes appropriate site selection, maximal sterile barrier precautions and chlorhexidine skin preparation during insertion, and prompt removal of central catheters that are no longer essential. Routine replacement solely to prevent infection is not recommended.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Prompt removal of unnecessary central catheters reduces exposure risk and is part of comprehensive CLABSI prevention; insertion and maintenance measures are distinct components.
candidate.source_document_title: Intravascular Catheter-related Infection Prevention Guidelines — Prevention Strategies and Summary of Recommendations
candidate.source_locator: Prevention Strategies: prompt removal of unnecessary central catheters identified during daily rounds; Summary Recommendations: maximal sterile barriers, >0.5% chlorhexidine with alcohol for CVC insertion; do not routinely replace CVCs solely to prevent infection
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
candidate.source_version_date: CDC web update April 12, 2024; current guidance accessed 2026
candidate.stem: During daily rounds, the nurse notes that a client's central venous catheter no longer has a current clinical indication. Which action is most consistent with central-line infection-prevention guidance?
